LESSON: READING 6.2.1 READING COMPREHENSION

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.2: Reading 6.2.1 Reading Comprehension
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 6.2.1 Reading Comprehension, part of Strand 6 in Grade 5 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: Why do we skim and scan texts?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. predict events in a text for comprehension,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 6.2.1 Reading Comprehension in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. skim and scan texts based on the theme for general and specific information,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 6.2.1 Reading Comprehension in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate skimming and scanning as key strategies in reading for lifelong learning.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 6.2.1 Reading Comprehension in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. predict events in a text for comprehension,

   Reading 6.2.1 Reading Comprehension helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. skim and scan texts based on the theme for general and specific information,

   Reading 6.2.1 Reading Comprehension helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. appreciate skimming and scanning as key strategies in reading for lifelong learning.

   Reading 6.2.1 Reading Comprehension helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. observe pictures and identify action words(verbs),

2. predict the events in a passage based on the title or picture clues,

3. skim through a passage to find the general idea of the story,

4. work jointly to scan through a passage to trace target vocabulary and verbs used,

5. conduct a reader’s theatre to practice reading texts clearly and fluently,

6. answer comprehension questions from texts read,

7. team up with peers to play a guessing game involving prediction of events in a story based on titles and picture clues.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. observe pictures and identify action words(verbs),
2. predict the events in a passage based on the title or picture clues,
3. skim through a passage to find the general idea of the story,
4. work jointly to scan through a passage to trace target vocabulary and verbs used,
5. conduct a reader’s theatre to practice reading texts clearly and fluently,
6. answer comprehension questions from texts read,
7. team up with peers to play a guessing game involving prediction of events in a story based on titles and picture clues.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 6.2.1 Reading Comprehension together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: This is promoted as the learner works jointly with peers to scan through a

passage to trace target vocabulary and verbs used.

• Self-efficacy: This is promoted as the learner shows concerted attention when conducting a reader’s theatre to

practice reading texts clearly and fluently.

Values:
• Peace: This is cultivated as the learner displays tolerance with peers when playing a guessing game involving prediction

of events in a story.

• Respect: This is portrayed as the learner accommodates diverse ideas when working with peers to predict the events in a

passage based on the title or picture clues.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Nationalism: This is enhanced as the learner is exposed to ideas and the thought of living harmoniously and respectfully with

people from special and vulnerable groups without discrimination.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the concept of skimming and scanning strategies acquired to their reading activities in English and

Kiswahili.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. predict events in a text for comprehension,
2. skim and scan texts based on the theme for general and specific information,
3. appreciate skimming and scanning as key strategies in reading for lifelong learning.

Remember the key question: Why do we skim and scan texts?
